blocks.title: DHCP and ARP
items: DHCP DORA: Discover (broadcast), Offer, Request, Acknowledge. Renewal starts at 50% of the lease (T1), rebind at 87.5% (T2).
A DHCP relay (`ip helper-address`) forwards broadcasts to a server on another subnet.
ARP maps IPv4 address to MAC on the local segment; gratuitous ARP announces or detects duplicates.
APIPA 169.254.x.x on a client means no DHCP server answered.

sheets.title: IP addressing
sheets.blurb: Special ranges, classes, the subnet table, IPv6.

blocks.title: Subnetting in four steps
items: Block size = 256 minus the interesting octet of the mask (for example /26: 256 - 192 = 64).
Network = the multiple of the block size at or below the host's value in that octet.
Broadcast = next network address minus 1; usable range sits between network and broadcast.
Hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2. Subnets = 2^(borrowed bits). Need N hosts: smallest 2^h with 2^h - 2 >= N.

head: Range

blocks.title: IPv6 address types
head: Type
Prefix
Notes
rows: Every interface; not routed; used by NDP and routing protocols
ff02::1 all nodes, ff02::2 all routers; no broadcast in IPv6

blocks.text: IPv6 is 128 bits written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits. Drop leading zeros in a group, and replace one run of all-zero groups with `::` (once only). Standard subnet is /64. SLAAC builds an address from the router's prefix plus an interface ID (EUI-64 or random); DHCPv6 can be stateful or stateless. NDP replaces ARP.

sheets.title: Troubleshooting
sheets.blurb: Method, commands, tools and common symptoms.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting method (CompTIA)
items: 1. Identify the problem (gather information, question users, duplicate it, check changes).
2. Establish a theory of probable cause (start simple; consider the OSI model).
3. Test the theory to determine the cause. If it fails, form a new theory or escalate.
4. Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects.
6. Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures.

blocks.title: Hardware tools
items: Cable tester: continuity and pinout. Toner and probe: find a cable in a bundle. TDR: distance to a copper break. OTDR: distance to a fiber break.
Loopback plug: tests a port. Wi-Fi analyzer: signal and channels. Protocol analyzer / packet sniffer: capture and decode traffic (Wireshark).
Crimper and punch-down tool for terminations; multimeter for voltage and continuity; optical power meter for fiber loss.
Pinouts: T568B is the common standard (orange pair first); a straight-through cable is the same standard on both ends, a crossover is T568A on one end and T568B on the other.
